title: group-roster - case shape (v0.2)
description: Pins the owner-signed group roster's TWO signature classes (decisions/protocol/0731 stage 2 and 0733; docs/spec/protocol.md 9.3.3). The frame is payload_len(u32 BE) || payload || ed25519_sig(64) || ml_dsa_65_sig(3309) in BOTH classes and the canonical payload is identical: what moves is the key that vouches for the roster, from the owner's person key under "myne.group-roster v1|" to one of the owner's devices under "myne.group-roster v2|". A reader MUST accept both and MUST resolve the device from an attestation it trusts: the owner_device field carried inside a person-signed group package, its own device key, or a verified vault.device-bindings row. Three case kinds: 'signed_bytes' (the exact message each class signs), 'verify' (the verdicts that separate the classes), 'package_payload' (the canonical package payload that carries or omits the attestation).

input_class.description: Which signature CLASS: v1 is the owner's person key, v2 is one of the owner's devices.

input_payload_hex.description: The canonical roster payload. IDENTICAL for both classes, which is the point: only the prefix differs.

expected_signed_bytes_hex.description: class prefix || payload. A port must reproduce this byte for byte to interoperate.

input_frame_hex.description: The whole signed frame, so a port exercises its own decoder rather than a payload it was handed.

input_owner_device_ed_pk_hex.description: The device half the reader was told to trust, or null for none.

expected_verified.description: The verdict. A person signature never satisfies a device verifier and vice versa, and a device with no attestation verifies nothing.

input_device_ed_pk_hex.description: The device half the reader was told to trust, or null for none. Null is the case that proves a roster carries no key of its own: the frame still parses, and verification refuses.

input_device_mldsa_vk_hex.description: The same device's ML-DSA-65 verifying key, or null.

input_payload_hex.description: One recipient's canonical group-key package payload, exactly as the person-signed package carries it.

expected_person_fingerprint_hex.description: The owner whose person signature covers the package.

expected_device_id_hex.description: Present when the payload carries the attestation.

expected_device_ed_pk_hex.description: The device half a recipient resolves out of the attested row.

expects_no_field.description: A field name that MUST be ABSENT from the canonical payload. 'owner_device' here: an absent attestation is omitted rather than null, so the bytes match the previous release exactly.
